drug_name: Dextroamphetamine Saccharate, Amphetamine Aspartate Monohydrate, Dextroamphetamine (Mixed Amphetamine Salts)
what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) in children, teenagers, and adults. It helps improve focus, attention, and control of behavior. It may also be used to treat narcolepsy, a sleep disorder that causes extreme daytime sleepiness.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. If you take the extended-release capsule (XR), swallow it whole. If you have trouble swallowing it, you may carefully open the capsule and sprinkle the beads onto a spoonful of applesauce, then swallow it right away without chewing. Never crush, chew, or break the extended-release capsule. Take your dose in the morning to help prevent trouble sleeping at night. If you take more than one dose per day, take the last dose no later than the early afternoon.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it to find the right amount for you. Do not change your dose on your own. For ADHD, adults and children 6 years and older typically start with a low dose once or twice daily. For narcolepsy, dosing varies by age and condition. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. This is a controlled substance, so your pharmacist can only give you a certain amount at a time, and you will need a new written prescription each time.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still early in the day. If it is late in the afternoon or evening, skip the missed dose and take your next dose as scheduled the following morning. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this could cause serious side effects.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine in a safe, locked place away from children and other people in your home. Amphetamines are a controlled substance and can be misused or stolen. Count your pills regularly. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist about a drug take-back program near you.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine in the afternoon or evening, as it can cause trouble sleeping. Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine. Avoid drinks or foods high in vitamin C (like orange juice or citrus fruits) around the time you take your dose, as they can reduce how well the medicine works. Do not take any new prescription, over-the-counter medicines, or supplements without telling your doctor first — especially antidepressants called MAOIs (such as phenelzine or tranylcypromine), as combining them can be dangerous. Avoid driving or doing activities that require focus until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: chest pain, shortness of breath, or fainting; fast or irregular heartbeat; high blood pressure; signs of circulation problems such as numbness, cold feeling, or color changes in your fingers or toes; new or worsening mental health symptoms such as hearing voices, seeing things, paranoia, aggression, or mood swings; signs of serotonin syndrome such as agitation, fast heart rate, high fever, muscle twitching, or nausea; seizures; or blurred vision. Also call your doctor if your child is not growing or gaining weight as expected, or if you notice any signs of misuse or dependence.
when_it_works: Many people begin to notice improvements in focus and attention within 30 minutes to 1 hour after taking a dose. The effects of the regular tablet last about 4 to 6 hours, while the extended-release capsule (XR) lasts about 10 to 12 hours. However, finding the right dose may take several weeks of adjustments with your doctor. Do not stop taking it on your own without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Children under 3 years old: This medicine is not approved for this age group. Children ages 3 to 5: Use is limited and only under close medical supervision. Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Using this medicine during pregnancy may harm the baby. Breastfeeding: This medicine passes into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Discuss the risks with your doctor. Elderly patients: Use with caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like heart problems or blood pressure changes. Heart conditions: Tell your doctor if you or any family member has a history of heart disease, heart defects, or sudden death, as this medicine can increase heart rate and blood pressure. History of substance use: Use with extreme caution if you or a family member has a history of drug or alcohol misuse, as this medicine has a high potential for dependence and misuse.
